sources.title: Introducing GPT-5.4
sources.evidence: Reopened October 27, 2026. The March 5 announcement identifies GPT-5.4 Thinking in ChatGPT and gpt-5.4 in the API, and describes reasoning, coding, vision, tool calling and native computer use. It gives no nominal total or active count. Incorporating GPT-5.3-Codex coding capabilities is not a size-bearing named-base relationship; neither pricing nor the 1M context statement supplies a parameter count.

sources.title: GPT-5.4 API model documentation
sources.evidence: Fresh October 27 API Markdown and official documentation fetch identify gpt-5.4-2026-03-05, text/image input, text output, 1,050,000 context, 128,000 maximum output, reasoning efforts none through xhigh, supported tools and prompt caching. Neither the complete model record nor its comparison table discloses total or active parameters.

sources.title: GPT-5.4 Thinking System Card
sources.evidence: Reopened October 27; the full 38-page PDF identifies GPT-5.4 Thinking, describes data and reinforcement-learning training in section 2, and reports safety/capability evaluations. Full extracted-text review found no nominal total or active parameter count or size-bearing base-model lineage. The mini appendix concerns a distinct variant and supplies no count for GPT-5.4.

sources.title: GPT-5.5 System Card
sources.evidence: Reopened October 27; the full April 23, 2026 GPT-5.5 card includes exact GPT-5.4 Thinking comparison columns for safety, health, cyber and monitorability. Complete extracted text and comparison tables report performance and response lengths, with no total/active parameter specification for GPT-5.4.

sources.title: Investigating the consequences of accidentally grading CoT during RL
sources.evidence: Reopened and freshly fetched October 27. The May 7 research identifies released GPT-5.4 Thinking among models affected by accidental CoT grading in RL; Figure 2 examines usefulness rewards and monitorability. The exact-model analysis contains no total/active count or size-bearing base-model relationship. GPT-5.4 Instant is separately discussed.

sources.title: Prompt Caching 201
sources.evidence: The guide explicitly applies to models before GPT-5.6 and describes OpenAI prompt caching using Transformer attention key/value projections. Combined with GPT-5.4 explicit caching support, it supports a qualified broad Transformer inference only, not dense/MoE topology or complete block composition.

sources.title: File inputs
sources.evidence: For vision-capable models, PDF input is processed into extracted text and page images. Responses supports PDF file input and Chat Completions accepts PDF files. This establishes an API document format when combined with the exact GPT-5.4 vision and endpoint support, not another native modality.

sources.title: OpenAI API changelog
sources.evidence: The March 5, 2026 entry releases GPT-5.4 to Chat Completions and Responses. March 13 documents an image-encoder bug fix for GPT-5.4 image inputs. June 1 extends distribution to Amazon Bedrock with regional feature differences. These are service history, not separate original release dates.

sources.title: OpenAI API deprecations
sources.evidence: The complete current page was checked for exact GPT-5.4 identifiers. It lists GPT-5.4 nano and GPT-5.4 Cyber notices but no shutdown notice for gpt-5.4 or gpt-5.4-2026-03-05. Sibling notices do not apply to this model, and documentation alone does not prove a live endpoint.

sources.title: OpenAI Services Agreement
sources.evidence: Section 9.1 reserves service intellectual-property rights and grants limited service use rather than ownership. Together with the exact hosted release, this supports a descriptive proprietary classification, not an open-weight license.

sources.title: OpenAI model inventory
sources.evidence: The inventory lists GPT-5.4 among hosted models. Its separate Open-weight section lists gpt-oss-120b and gpt-oss-20b with Apache 2.0. The checked exact release and documentation provide no downloadable GPT-5.4 weights.

sources.title: Models.dev GPT-5.4 record
sources.evidence: The original catalog lead was inspected from its current raw file. Its generic family and promotional description were not treated as primary evidence; its context and modality claims were checked independently.

sources.title: Much Ado about Prompting: LLM Classification of Text Messages from Experiments
sources.publisher: Can Çelebi and Stefan P. Penczynski
sources.evidence: Original June 16, 2026 empirical paper freshly reopened October 27; section 5.2 and Table 1 on PDF page 9 were read and visually inspected. The exact GPT 5.4 row has separate Total and Active columns, both dashes; the text and footnote explicitly say its counts are not disclosed. This corroborates the gap as an independent research comparison, not an OpenAI disclosure. The Qwen counts and dense-model convention do not transfer to GPT-5.4.

sources.title: Incompressible Knowledge Probes: Estimating Black-Box LLM Parameter Counts via Factual Capacity
sources.evidence: Original April 27, 2026 paper reopened October 27 after the author companion site surfaced in fresh search. Section 4.4 estimates size by inverting an accuracy calibration; Appendix D leaves the exact gpt-5.4 Params entry blank. Appendix I explicitly characterizes estimates as effective capacity, not literal architecture. Its black-box estimates and inferred family relationships are not published nominal model specifications or active-weight counts, so neither parameter field is filled from them.

name.note: Official API display name; GPT-5.4 Thinking is the corresponding ChatGPT name.

developer.note: Identified by the developer announcement and system card.

family.note: Normalize to the named GPT-5.4 generation. This does not imply shared weights with mini, nano, Pro or Instant.

release_date.note: Explicit public launch across ChatGPT, Codex and API. The March 13 encoder fix and June 1 additional provider availability do not move the original release date.

open_weights.note: Hosted model distribution under reserved service IP; checked official sources provide no downloadable weights for this model.

license.note: Descriptive hosted-service classification; not a claimed SPDX identifier or downloadable-weight license.

parameters_b.note: Fresh October 27 re-audit reopened the launch, current API record, full original and later comparison cards, and exact-model RL research. No nominal total or size-bearing named-base relationship was found. The June 16 original classification study explicitly leaves GPT-5.4 Total blank. Fresh parameter-disclosure and original-research searches found no supported later count; IKP estimates effective knowledge capacity rather than literal weights.

active_parameters_b.note: Rechecked separately October 27. No explicit active count appears in the original/later OpenAI evidence; the June 16 study has a separate Active column and leaves GPT-5.4 blank. No exact-model active-count convention was established by the fresh original-research comparison search. IKP capacity estimates, sibling values and dense total-equals-active assumptions cannot supply this field.

architecture.note: Qualified cross-source inference: exact GPT-5.4 documentation supports prompt caching, and OpenAI pre-GPT-5.6 caching documentation describes Transformer attention KV state. This is a broad classification only. Original/later cards and exact-model training/interpretability searches did not establish full block composition, dense/MoE topology or layer counts.

context_window.note: Exact API context is 1,050,000 tokens, with 128,000 maximum output. Do not derive an independent input ceiling by subtraction or substitute product-specific ChatGPT/Codex launch limits. Endpoint operation was not tested.

modalities.note: Text/image are native inputs and text is the output. PDF is retained as an API-supported input format converted into extracted text and page images. Hosted image-generation tool support does not establish native image output.

reasoning.note: Exact API documentation exposes reasoning tokens with none, low, medium, high and xhigh effort. The none default does not negate reasoning capability; the card and later RL research independently describe its internal reasoning training.

tool_call.note: Exact model documentation explicitly supports function calling and tools including computer use; not inferred from a sibling.

description.value: OpenAI reasoning model for coding and general tasks, with text and image input, tool calling and computer use.

patch.notes: Released March 5, 2026 in ChatGPT as GPT-5.4 Thinking, Codex and the API; the API default snapshot is gpt-5.4-2026-03-05. The API context is 1,050,000 tokens with a 128,000-token maximum output; ChatGPT and Codex product limits differ. OpenAI documented an image-encoder fix on March 13. PDF means API extraction into text and page images, and hosted image generation is a tool rather than native model output. Transformer is a qualified broad inference from exact-model prompt caching support and OpenAI pre-GPT-5.6 KV-cache documentation. Detailed topology and total/active parameter counts remain undisclosed in the checked sources; a later original study also leaves both counts blank. Black-box knowledge-capacity estimates are not model weight counts. No exact-model API shutdown notice was found in the current deprecation page; live endpoint operation was not tested.

summary: Parameter-only re-audit on October 27 reopened the launch, current API documentation, full original/later OpenAI cards and exact-model RL research, and searched for later disclosures and original active-count comparisons. The June 16 classification study explicitly leaves GPT-5.4 total and active counts blank; IKP estimates effective knowledge capacity rather than literal parameters. Both counts remain null/undisclosed with explicit null patches. The other 12 field assessments are unchanged.
